note: Rules a static guard cannot decide. Each names the document it comes from; docs/factory/rule-coverage.md lists what enforces every rule. Sync with tools/factory/sync_rules.py (creates missing rules by name, never edits or deletes).

rules.name: Keynes: simulation results must not depend on timing or load
rules.content: Check that production, consumption, price updates, planning cadence and command effective dates are decided only by the seed, content version, sealed command log and game day. Wall-clock time, frame rate, thread wake-ups, slice budgets or machine load may change when work finishes, never what it produces.
rules.bad_examples:
if Time.get_ticks_msec() - _last_plan_ms > 500:
    _run_planning(day)  # result depends on machine speed

rules.name: Keynes: the front end only reads published frames
rules.source: AGENTS.md; docs/architecture/module-map.md#十二域以外 (显示与界面)
rules.content: Code under scripts/ui and scripts/rendering may read only the published, committed frame and forward player requests to the simulation. It must not read live simulation state to make decisions and must not write simulation state; the simulation decides where it stops to wait for the player.
rules.bad_examples:
if economy_runtime.cash_of(id) < cost:
    economy_runtime.add_cash(id, cost)  # UI deciding and writing state

rules.name: Keynes: cross-module hand-offs go through committed views or intents
rules.content: A module reads another module only through the owner's committed view (copy_committed_view / observe_committed_view) and changes it only by submitting an intent the owner accepts. Reject code that keeps a reference to another owner's snapshot or plan, holds its writable container, or patches its money, goods or population directly, including through pointers or aliases the text guards miss.
rules.bad_examples:
CountryState& s = country->mutable_state();
s.treasury += refund;  // writes another owner's state

rules.name: Keynes: new continuation state is versioned, validated and installed atomically
rules.content: When a change adds state that affects later days (fractional remainders, per-cell dates, request or ACK cursors, id counters), check that its owner freezes a copy at the commit boundary, bumps the section version, validates length, finiteness and content identity, decodes completely before installing, and rejects older versions with an explicit error. Saving only a cursor or a display mirror is not enough.
rules.bad_examples: _rain_remainder = bytes.decode_float(off)  # installed while decoding, no version bump, old saves default to 0

rules.name: Keynes: fix the root cause instead of relaxing the check
rules.content: Flag changes that make a failing test or replay pass by loosening assertions, widening tolerances, lengthening timeouts, adding retries, running more days, deleting compared fields or changing a hash algorithm. A fix must come with root-cause evidence (reproduction, log or code path) and keep the original comparison.
rules.good_examples: assert_eq(restored_hash, live_hash)  # kept, the save now includes the missing cursor
rules.bad_examples:
await wait_days(20)  # was 8; passes by waiting longer
assert_true(abs(a - b) < 1000)  # was assert_eq(a, b)

rules.name: Keynes: errors fail loudly instead of falling back silently
rules.content: When something goes wrong (a missing extension or method, a failed native call, invalid or missing data, an unexpected state, a failed load or decode), report it with push_error or an explicit error result, stop that operation and keep the previous state. Do not silently switch to another code path, a default value, an empty result or a GDScript reimplementation, and do not report success. A fallback is acceptable only where the docs name it as intended behaviour, and it must still log the cause. Defaults for values that are documented as optional are fine; flag a default only when it hides data or a result that must exist. The climate entry points in map_generator.gd (Pass-A, Pass-B, ocean, sea-ice, transpiration) have no fallback at all: no GDScript full-map computation and no successful empty result.

rules.name: Keynes: daily stage functions stay engine-free
rules.content: native_simulation_stage_<domain>.cpp functions run on both the inline path and the worker thread, so they must not touch Godot objects, resources or the GPU. Their bool return means continue traversal, not business success; success, waiting and failure stay in the existing stage/commit fields and fault state.
rules.good_examples:
stage.result = StageResult::Waiting;
return true;  // keep traversing; the wait is recorded in the stage
rules.bad_examples:
Ref<Image> img = Image::create(w, h, false, Image::FORMAT_RF);  // Godot object on the worker
return ok;  // bool used as business result

rules.name: Keynes: saves happen only at a committed boundary and never lose commands
rules.content: Saving must wait for a committed safe boundary through GameSaveCoordinator and must not capture Plan intermediates from a provider. Commands beyond the PKSR capacity must fail explicitly and keep every command. A failed load must not switch to a new world or continue a half-restored session.
rules.good_examples:
if pending.size() > PKSR_COMMAND_CAPACITY:
    return fail("save: %d pending commands exceed capacity" % pending.size())
rules.bad_examples: pending = pending.slice(0, PKSR_COMMAND_CAPACITY)  # silently drops commands

rules.name: Keynes: background-day tests wait for the committed day and receive results
rules.source: docs/architecture/development-guide.md#存档 (手动推进后台日的测试)
rules.content: Tests that advance background days manually must wait with wait_for_runtime_day for the committed date and run the production result-receive step (e.g. the host's _service_runtime_liveness) before asserting. Waiting only until the observed day grows, or using 'one more day after observing' as the completion condition, is wrong.

rules.name: Keynes: session components get narrow dependencies and one daily entry
rules.content: Components split out of world_runtime_host.gd receive narrow Callable or RefCounted dependencies, never the whole host, and never add a second daily-advance entry. Callbacks handed to signals or save services must be Callables bound to the host, not the component's own unbound methods.
rules.bad_examples:
_daily = WorldRuntimeDailyAdapter.new(host)
save_service.on_saved = Callable(self, "_on_saved")  # component method, not host-bound

rules.name: Keynes: GDScript splits keep the public surface and literals
rules.content: When splitting a GDScript file, public methods and signals stay in the original file as thin forwards and responsibilities move to RefCounted collaborators (pure transforms to static helpers), not extends chains. Adding a host. prefix must not change string literals or comments, and Callable(self, ...) or method names passed as values must still point at the host.
rules.bad_examples:
extends "res://scripts/ui/game_ui_manager_base.gd"
emit_signal("host.day_changed")  # prefix leaked into a literal

rules.name: Keynes: shaders keep if-branches few and are judged by real GPU work
rules.content: Use as few if statements in shaders as possible. Pixels in one batch that take different branches often execute both paths, so a branch rarely saves work and can cost it. Do not count an if-branch as saved work. There is no fixed pattern for shader optimisation: first measure where the GPU actually spends its time, then change that, and justify a claimed speed-up with measured frame time at the same quality and resolution.

rules.name: Keynes: treasury construction checks the regime capability
rules.content: Economy construction quote and apply must both reject requests from a country whose frozen CountryReadView lacks CountryApi::CAP_TREASURY_CONSTRUCTION. Regime state belongs to Country and must not be written to HexCell, DataCore or the Ideology POD; restoring an old save must not default to allowing treasury construction.
rules.bad_examples:
// quote checks the capability, apply does not
return apply_construction(request);

rules.name: Keynes: gates are tested with inputs they must refuse
rules.content: A new or changed gate, parser, allowlist or validator in tools/factory/ (or any code that decides whether something may proceed) must come with a test that feeds it an input it has to refuse: malformed, empty, unknown, or carrying extra syntax. Tests that only show good input being accepted do not count. Unknown values must be refused, not read as clean, and the function must be listed in GATES in tools/factory/tests/test_gates_refuse.py.
rules.good_examples: GATES["native_line"] = [("a second command after ;", lambda: not native_line(SCRIPT + " ; rm x", SCRIPT))]
rules.bad_examples: def test_native_line(): assert native_line(SCRIPT + " --flag", SCRIPT)  # only the accepted case
